result:
Perfect! The test fails as expected. The actual output is `"https://example.com/apgraphql1https://example.com/api/v1"` instead of the expected `"https://example.com/graphql/v1"`, which confirms the bug in the `filterNewLine` transaction filter. The filter is incorrectly reconstructing the document when handling paste events.

Here's the JSON result:

```json
{
  "testFilePath": "packages/altair-app/src/app/modules/altair/components/x-input/x-input.repro.spec.ts",
  "expectedBehavior": "When pasting 'graphql' to replace a selected 'api' substring in the URL 'https://example.com/api/v1', only the selected portion should be replaced, resulting in 'https://example.com/graphql/v1'",
  "actualBehavior": "The paste transaction filter incorrectly reconstructs the entire document from position 0, producing corrupted output: 'https://example.com/apgraphql1https://example.com/api/v1', instead of preserving the original transaction's from/to positions and only sanitizing the inserted text"
}
```
